---
title: "JAXCMR"
description: "Analyze recall, fit memory-search models, and compare simulated and observed behavior."
---

JAXCMR is a Python library for studying memory search with computational models,
including Context Maintenance and Retrieval (CMR). It brings together recall
analyses, model specification, parameter estimation and simulation, so researchers
can develop an account of memory and compare its predictions with observed behavior.

Its CMR implementations combine components for context, associative memory and
recall termination. Shared interfaces connect models to fitting and simulation,
making it possible to investigate alternative mechanisms within an existing
workflow. [JAX](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/jit-compilation.html) compiles
numerical calculations for repeated execution; the documented workflows use
CPU computation.

## Start with fitting

**[Fitting a model](templates/fitting_scipyde.ipynb)** brings the main activities
together in one notebook: load observed recalls, estimate model parameters,
simulate recall from the fitted model, and apply the same behavioral analyses
to the observations and simulations. It saves the fit, simulated responses and
comparison figures for subsequent work.

The worked example uses the **war-photo-recall experiment**. Read its saved
results to follow the procedure, then use the notebook's **parameters** cell
to configure your own run. The [Templates introduction](templates.qmd#from-a-template-to-a-run)
explains input files, settings, execution and saved outputs.

## Choose where to run it

- **[VS Code on your Mac](getting-started.qmd):** install Python and create a
  notebook environment. The instructions assume an Apple Silicon Mac and no
  previous Python experience. This route awaits the planned 0.2.0 PyPI release.
- **[Colab in your browser](templates.qmd#run-in-colab):** use a template's
  **Open in Colab** link. Its setup cell installs the library and fetches the
  example inputs; the instructions explain saving your work and the current
  status of the supplied examples.

## Explore the library

- **[Library Guide](overview/index.qmd):** data structures, interfaces and
  extension points for understanding and adapting workflows.
- **[Templates](templates.qmd):** fourteen complete procedures, including
  individual recall analyses, simulation, parameter exploration and model comparison.
- **[Repository](https://github.com/githubpsyche/jaxcmr):** source code, tests
  and research material, including additional notebooks with varying maintenance status.
